predict.title: No null check
options: It shows **3 products**
It throws a `NullReferenceException`
It shows **0 products**, then **3 products**
It shows nothing until the data arrives
predict.explanation: Blazor renders the component **before** the `await` finishes. At that moment `products` is still `null`, so `products.Count` throws a `NullReferenceException`. Check for `null` first and show **Loading...** (`@if (products is null)`).

predict.title: A POST that fails
options: **Save failed.**
Nothing: the exception is not caught
**Saved!**
An error UI: 400 crashes the component
predict.explanation: **Saved!** `PostAsJsonAsync` returns the `HttpResponseMessage` and does **not** throw on a 400 or 500. It only throws when the request can't be sent at all (for example, no network). Keep the response and call `response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` or check `response.IsSuccessStatusCode`.

predict.title: [Authorize] on a child
predict.body:
AdminTools.razor (no `@page`): ```razor @attribute [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")] ``` The home page uses it: ```razor @page "/"

Home

``` The router uses `AuthorizeRouteView`. A user who is **not logged in** opens `/`. **What do they see?**
options: **Home** and the **Delete everything** button
**Home** only
A redirect to the login page
A build error: `[Authorize]` needs `@page`
predict.explanation: `[Authorize]` is only checked on **routable components** (pages), by `AuthorizeRouteView`. On a child component it is **ignored**, so the button shows for everyone. To hide part of a page, wrap it in `<AuthorizeView Roles="Admin">`.

predict.title: The wrong role
predict.body:
```razor
<AuthorizeView Roles="Admin">
    <Authorized>Delete</Authorized>
    <NotAuthorized>Read only</NotAuthorized>
</AuthorizeView>
```

Bo is **logged in**. His only role is **Editor**.

**What does Bo see?**
options: **Delete**, because he is logged in
**Delete** and **Read only**
Nothing, because he has a role but not the right one
**Read only**
predict.explanation: With `Roles="Admin"`, being logged in is not enough: the user must be in the **Admin** role. Bo fails the check, so `<NotAuthorized>` renders: **Read only**. `NotAuthorized` covers both "not logged in" and "logged in but not allowed".

practice.title: Register HttpClient in WebAssembly
practice.task:
In the WebAssembly project's `Program.cs`, register an **`HttpClient`** as a **scoped** service, so components can `@inject HttpClient Http` and call relative URLs like `"api/products"`.

Its **`BaseAddress`** must be the address of the site itself: `builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress`.

checks.label: Still builds and runs the app
checks.hint: Keep `await builder.Build().RunAsync();` as the last line.

practice.title: Loading, error, and data
practice.task:
This page crashes on the first render and when the API is down. Fix it: 1. Add a **`private string? error;`** field. 2. Wrap the call in **`try/catch`**, catch **`HttpRequestException`**, and set `error` to `"Could not load the products."`. 3. In the markup: if `error` is not `null`, show it. Else, if `products` is `null`, show **`

Loading...

`**. Else show the list.
practice.hint: Put the `GetFromJsonAsync` line inside `try { }`, and add `catch (HttpRequestException) { error = "..."; }`. In the markup use `@if (error is not null) { } else if (products is null) { } else { }`.

checks.label: The call is inside a `try` block
Catches `HttpRequestException` and sets `error`
checks.hint: Add `catch (HttpRequestException) { error = "Could not load the products."; }`.

checks.label: Shows `error` when it is not `null`
checks.hint:
Start the markup with `@if (error is not null) {

@error

}`.

practice.title: Check the POST response
practice.task:
This method always shows **Saved!**, even when the API answers 400 or 500, because `PostAsJsonAsync` doesn't throw on an error status.

1. Keep the result in a variable called **`response`**.
2. Use **`response.IsSuccessStatusCode`** (or `EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` with a `try/catch`) so the message is **`Saved!`** on success and **`Save failed.`** otherwise.

checks.label: Keeps the result: `var response = await Http.PostAsJsonAsync(...)`
Sets `message` to `"Save failed."` on failure
checks.hint: In the failure branch, write `message = "Save failed.";`.

practice.title: Show and hide with AuthorizeView
practice.task:
Right now everyone sees everything. Change the menu:

1. Wrap the first part in **`<AuthorizeView>`**: logged-in users see **`Hello, @context.User.Identity?.Name!`** (in `<Authorized>`), others see the **login** link (in `<NotAuthorized>`).
2. Wrap the **admin** link in a second `<AuthorizeView>` with **`Roles="Admin"`**.
practice.hint: Inside `<Authorized>`, `context` is the `AuthenticationState`, so the name is `@context.User.Identity?.Name`.

checks.label: The admin link is inside `<AuthorizeView Roles="Admin">`
No more `userName` field
checks.hint: Read the name from `context.User`, and delete the `userName` field.

practice.title: Protect the page and the API
practice.task:
A Blazor WebAssembly app has an admin page and an API endpoint. Protect **both** for the **Admin** role:

1. In `Admin.razor`, add **`@attribute [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]`** below `@page`.
2. In the server's `Program.cs`, add **`.RequireAuthorization(...)`** to the `MapDelete` endpoint so only the Admin role can call it. (The page check runs in the browser and can be bypassed; the API check can't.)
practice.hint: `.RequireAuthorization()` takes a policy builder: `.RequireAuthorization(p => p.RequireRole("Admin"))`. A named policy (`.RequireAuthorization("AdminOnly")`) also works if you defined it.

checks.label: The page still has `@page "/admin"`
checks.hint: Keep `@page "/admin"`: `[Authorize]` only works on routable components.

practice.title: Read the user in code, from scratch
practice.task:
Write **`DeleteButton.razor`** (a component, not a page):

- A **cascading parameter** `Task<AuthenticationState>` called **`AuthenticationStateTask`**.
- In **`OnInitializedAsync`**, **await** it, get the `User`, and set a `private bool isAdmin` to `true` only if the user **is authenticated** and **is in the `Admin` role**.
- Render `<button>Delete</button>` only when `isAdmin` is `true`.
practice.hint: `[CascadingParameter] private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }`, then `var user = (await AuthenticationStateTask).User;`.

checks.label: A `[CascadingParameter]` of type `Task<AuthenticationState>`
checks.hint: Add `[CascadingParameter] private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }`.

checks.label: Awaits the task in `OnInitializedAsync`
checks.hint: Inside `protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()`, write `var authState = await AuthenticationStateTask;`.

quiz.body: An AI tool wrote a Blazor **WebAssembly** component that opens a `SqlConnection` with a connection string. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, as long as the connection string is in `appsettings.json`
It only needs `@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly` to work
The code runs in the browser: the connection string would be public, and the browser can't connect to the database. It should call a server API
It should use `SqlConnection` in `OnAfterRenderAsync` instead
quiz.explanation: WebAssembly code is downloaded and runs in the **user's browser**. Everything in it (including config files in `wwwroot`) is visible, and the browser can't open a database connection. The path is browser → HTTP → **server API** → database.

quiz.body: `await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<Product>("api/products/99")` and the API answers **404 Not Found**. What happens?
options: It throws an `HttpRequestException`
It returns `null`
It returns an empty `Product`
It returns the `HttpResponseMessage`
quiz.explanation: `GetFromJsonAsync<T>` checks the status for you and **throws `HttpRequestException`** on a non-success status. It returns `null` only when the body is the JSON `null`. Catch the exception to show an error message.

quiz.body: `var response = await Http.PostAsJsonAsync("api/orders", order);` and the API answers **500**. What is true?
options: An `HttpRequestException` is thrown at this line
`response` is `null`
The order is sent again automatically
No exception: `response.IsSuccessStatusCode` is `false`
quiz.explanation: `PostAsJsonAsync` returns the response and **doesn't throw** on an error status. Check `response.IsSuccessStatusCode`, or call `response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode()`, which throws if the status is not 2xx.

quiz.body: A WebAssembly app at `https://app.example.com` calls `https://api.example.com/products`. The browser console says the request was **blocked by CORS policy**. Where is the fix?
options: In the Blazor app: set a header on the `HttpClient`
In the **API**: allow the origin `https://app.example.com` with CORS (`AddCors` / `UseCors`)
In the browser settings of each user
Switch the component to `InteractiveAuto`
quiz.explanation: CORS is enforced by the browser, but **allowed by the server**. The API must send headers that allow your app's origin. Nothing in the Blazor client can turn it off. An API on the same origin doesn't need CORS.

options: Content for users who are allowed
Content shown **while the authentication state is still loading**
Content for users with any role
A login form
quiz.explanation: `Authorizing` shows while Blazor is still getting the `AuthenticationState` (for example, in WebAssembly while it loads). Then it switches to `Authorized` or `NotAuthorized`.

quiz.body: You put `@attribute [Authorize]` on `UserMenu.razor`, a component **without `@page`** that is used in the layout. An anonymous user opens the site. What happens?
options: The menu is hidden
The user is redirected to login
A build error
The menu renders anyway: `[Authorize]` is ignored on non-page components
quiz.explanation: `[Authorize]` is only checked for **routable components**, by the router (`AuthorizeRouteView`) or the endpoint. For part of a page, use `<AuthorizeView>`.

options: The user is in **Admin or Manager** (any of them)
The user is in **both** Admin and Manager
The user is in a role named `Admin,Manager`
Only that the user is logged in
quiz.explanation: A comma-separated `Roles` list means **any** of these roles is enough. To require both, nest two `AuthorizeView`s or use a policy.

quiz.body: A component reads the user in code. Which is correct?
options: `@inject ClaimsPrincipal User` and use `User` directly
`[Parameter] public AuthenticationState Auth { get; set; }`
`[CascadingParameter] Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }`, then `(await AuthenticationStateTask).User`
`HttpContext.User`, which works in every render mode
quiz.explanation: With `AddCascadingAuthenticationState()` registered, every component can receive a cascading **`Task<AuthenticationState>`**. Await it to get the `User`. `HttpContext` is not available in interactive components.

quiz.body: A page has `@attribute [Authorize]`, but in the interactive app anonymous users can still open it by clicking a link. The router has `<RouteView RouteData="routeData" ... />`. What is the fix?
options: Add `[Authorize]` to `MainLayout` too
Remove `@page` from the protected page
Wrap the page content in `<NotAuthorized>`
Replace `RouteView` with **`AuthorizeRouteView`**
quiz.explanation: `RouteView` just renders the page. **`AuthorizeRouteView`** checks `[Authorize]` before rendering, and shows its `<NotAuthorized>` content when the check fails.

quiz.body: A WebAssembly app hides the **Delete** button with `<AuthorizeView Roles="Admin">`. The API endpoint `DELETE /api/products/{id}` has no authorization. Is it safe?
options: No: anyone can call the API directly or change the client code. The API must require the Admin role too
Yes: non-admins never see the button
Yes, if the page also has `[Authorize]`
Yes, because WebAssembly code is compiled and can't be changed
quiz.explanation: Client checks are **user experience**, not security. The user controls the browser: they can call the endpoint with any HTTP tool. Protect the endpoint with `[Authorize]` or `.RequireAuthorization()`.

interview.question: How do you call a web API from a Blazor component?
interview.modelAnswer: Inject `HttpClient` (or a service that wraps it) and use the JSON helpers: `GetFromJsonAsync<T>` to read, `PostAsJsonAsync` to send. Call it in `OnInitializedAsync` or an event handler, show a loading state while the result is `null`, and handle errors with `try/catch` and the status code.

interview.question: How should you create an `HttpClient` on the server, and why?
interview.modelAnswer: Through `IHttpClientFactory`, usually as a typed client registered with `AddHttpClient<MyClient>(c => c.BaseAddress = ...)`. The factory reuses and refreshes the underlying connections, so you avoid running out of sockets or keeping stale DNS, which can happen when you `new HttpClient()` everywhere.

interview.question: Why does a Blazor WebAssembly app need a web API for its data?
interview.modelAnswer: Because its code runs in the user's browser. The browser can't connect to a database, and any secret like a connection string would be public. So the client calls an HTTP API on the server, and only the server talks to the database. If the API is on another origin, the API must allow it with CORS.

interview.question: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
interview.modelAnswer: Authentication is finding out who the user is, for example by logging in; the result is a `ClaimsPrincipal` with claims. Authorization is deciding what that user may do, by checking roles, claims or policies. In Blazor, ASP.NET Core handles authentication, and components use the result to authorize.

interview.question: How does a component know who the current user is?
interview.modelAnswer: `AuthenticationStateProvider` gives the `AuthenticationState`. With `AddCascadingAuthenticationState()`, it is cascaded as a `Task<AuthenticationState>`. A component takes it as a `[CascadingParameter]`, awaits it, and reads `User`: `Identity.IsAuthenticated`, `Identity.Name`, `IsInRole`. In markup, `AuthorizeView` does this for you.

interview.question: When do you use `AuthorizeView` and when `[Authorize]`?
interview.modelAnswer: `[Authorize]` protects a whole page: it only works on components with `@page`, and the router's `AuthorizeRouteView` enforces it. `AuthorizeView` shows or hides part of the markup, with `Authorized`, `NotAuthorized` and `Authorizing` content, and optional `Roles` or `Policy`.

interview.question: An Auto component loads data. How do you make it work both on the server and in the browser?
interview.modelAnswer: Hide the data access behind an interface, like `IProductService`. Register an implementation that uses `HttpClient` to call the API in the client project, and one that reads the database directly in the server project. The component only injects the interface, so it works during server prerendering and after it moves to WebAssembly.

interview.question: Is hiding a button with `AuthorizeView` in a WebAssembly app enough to secure an action?
interview.modelAnswer: No. The client code runs in the user's browser and can be changed or skipped, and anyone can call the API directly. Hiding UI is only for user experience. The API must enforce authorization with `[Authorize]` or `.RequireAuthorization()`.
